analysis.reply_text: First, move closer to your router and watch if the drops stop, because that helps you rule out weak signal or interference. Next, restart the router by unplugging it for about 20 seconds, then plug it back in and wait for it to fully reconnect. Then, on your device, toggle Wi-Fi off and on, and forget the network and rejoin if needed. After that, check for router firmware updates in its app or web page, and update if one is available. Also try changing the Wi-Fi channel or switching between 2.4 gigahertz and 5 gigahertz to reduce interference from neighbors or smart devices. Finally, if it still drops, connect with an Ethernet cable to test stability, and if that works, it points to a Wi-Fi configuration or hardware issue, so consider resetting or replacing the router.
